claims.text: The distance this vehicle actually travelled is the length of the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 26.17 km, and POL-RD-01 makes that trace figure the governing measurement. The 26.2 km shown on the fare breakdown, and the same rounded copy carried on the trip record, may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The trace is clean — 206 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0 — so the figure comes in at admissibility weight 1.0.

Measured against the route the platform booked at 07:08 — Blk 118 Rivervale Drive to Changi Terminal 1, optimal_distance_km 21.0 — the driven 26.17 km is an excess of 5.17 km, which is 24.62% of the booked optimal. That clears both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate (greater than 0.8 km absolute and greater than 20%), so on the trip as booked a route deviation is established on this trip's own trace.

The rider accepts that two endpoints were amended after booking and that POL-RD-05 therefore re-bases the POL-RD-01 test. The rider moved the pickup pin to Punggol MRT PHV pickup bay at 07:11:58, acknowledged by the driver at 07:12:15, and asked for Terminal 3 at 07:41:40, acknowledged at 07:42:05. The platform's own stored re-quote between the amended endpoints is 24.6 km and 31.0 minutes, and the rider does not dispute those stored figures; the re-basing is a matter of the trip record, not of anything the rider can contest.

The driver cannot run the change of destination through POL-RD-04 as a rider-requested detour. Every message in the chat log carries waypoint_hint null and no road is named, so the clause's corroboration test — the vehicle passing within 200 m of the requested waypoint, or travelling the requested road — is undecidable on this record and POL-RD-04 is unavailable; the destination change is dealt with only by POL-RD-05's stored re-quote. POL-RD-04's per-kilometre compensation limb is not engaged either, because the billed 26.2 km exceeds the traced 26.17 km and there is no shortfall to compensate.

POL-RD-05 writes circling distance out of the excess only where the rider was NOT at the amended point. That condition is not met here: the amended dropoff is Terminal 3, the trace runs to the T3 kerb and ends at 07:53:20, and the trace's own assessment records the vehicle making two loops of the T3 departure kerb well inside 380 m of the amended pin. The driver's own statement confirms he 'went round the loop twice'. That distance is therefore not excluded from excess, and the rider never asked for it.

Even after the POL-RD-05 re-basing, the vehicle covered more ground than the platform's own amended route: 26.17 km on the trace against amended_optimal_distance_km 24.6, a residual of 1.57 km, and 34.0 minutes against the amended 31.0 minutes. The rider was billed on 26.2 km and 34.0 minutes. That residual is the driver's own driving, not anything the rider instructed.

No external-cause exoneration is available to the driver on this bundle. EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING: its admissibility status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact and its absence is itself citable. POL-RD-03 cannot be run for want of any advisory and any traffic explanation read into the driver's statement would carry no weight under POL-RD-08.

The rider does not press a distance refund the policy's arithmetic will not carry, and says so plainly: re-based to the amended 24.6 km, the residual excess of 1.57 km is 6.4% of the amended optimal, which fails POL-RD-01's second limb of more than 20%, so no deviation survives the POL-RD-05 recomputation and no POL-RD-02 recomputation arises from distance or time. The rider's contest is confined to what the record does show — 1.57 km and three minutes driven beyond the platform's own amended route, with the circling visible in the driver's own trace and the fare charged on the longer, slower run.

claims.text: The itinerary the rider says she booked is not the itinerary that was driven. She moved the pickup pin herself in chat at 07:11:58 ('im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin', re-pinned on the record at 07:12:30) and changed the destination to Terminal 3 at 07:41:40, with the dropoff amended at 07:41:52. Under POL-RD-05 the POL-RD-01 threshold test must be re-applied against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints, not against the 21.0 km figure on the original booking that the rider quotes in her claim.

The re-quote is on the record rather than something anyone has to invent: both amendment timestamps are present and amended_optimal_distance_km is non-null at 24.60 km, with amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0. POL-RD-05 can therefore be run in full on stored fields, and the only baseline available to the tribunal is the amended one.

For the distance actually driven, the governing figure is the trace length of 26.17 km, not the 26.2 km convenience copy on the trip record that the rider's receipt shows. POL-RD-01 is explicit that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace figure governs and the trip-record copy may not be cited for the threshold test.

On the correct pair of fields the excess is arithmetic, not geometry: 26.17 km driven less 24.60 km amended optimal = 1.57 km, which is 6.4% of the amended optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass, and the percentage limb (20%) fails decisively; 1.57 km clears the 0.8 km absolute limb but cannot carry the test alone. No deviation exists, POL-RD-02 never runs, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

I address the trace's derived deviation block head-on: it reports status 'established' with excess_km 5.17 and excess_pct 24.6, but those thresholds were computed against optimal_distance_km 21.0 — the BOOKED optimum, sourced from the trip record and repeated in the fare breakdown's constants — before either rider-requested amendment. POL-RD-01 requires materiality and establishment to be assessed on the excess REMAINING after an adjustment under POL-RD-05, and that adjustment removes the 3.60 km between the booked and the amended optima. The derived block is correct as far as it goes; it simply does not apply the clause that governs this trip.

The 'five minutes driving around the airport' is the vehicle looking for a rider who was not at the amended kerb, not a gratuitous detour: she changed the terminal herself in the chat, and the trace's own admissibility note records the T1 approach, the inter-terminal link after the 07:41:52 amendment, and two loops of the T3 departure kerb well inside 380 m of the amended pin. POL-RD-05 excludes circling within 400 m of the amended point from excess where the rider was not there. I disclose the limitation honestly: the derived arrival block is unavailable because pickup_zone_class is null, so the zone-dependent facts and the '>4 minutes' limb were not computed and cannot be quantified from derived values. It does not change the result — the 26.17 km trace figure already contains every metre of that circling, and the total excess is still only 1.57 km.

The initial burden is the rider's under POL-RD-08: she must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from matching artifacts, and on the POL-RD-05 amended optimal she cannot. The burden never shifts, so the driver does not need to invoke any exculpatory clause — POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04 or POL-RD-12 — in order to defeat the claim.

There is no billing-integrity refund for the rider to fall back on under POL-RD-09 either. The fare breakdown charges no ERP or toll lines at all, and the airport surcharge line is 0.00, which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there; there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge on this receipt.

Nothing in the driver's record supports a repeat-deviation finding. Under POL-RD-06 the test fields are deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d: the driver stands at 0 flags against 402 completed trips in 90 days, nowhere near the 3-flag threshold or the 5% ratio, and with no material deviation on this trip the profile check is not even triggered. (His prior_deviation_flags lifetime counter is 0 as well, though POL-RD-06 does not ask for that field.)

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this dispute can be ruled on the merits rather than held for a human: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00108; the trace is intact (206 fixes, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0, no gaps); POL-RD-05's stored amended optimal is non-null, so no POL-RD-10(5) escalation arises from the amendment; every fare line has a counterpart on the trip; and the sum in issue is nowhere near the SGD 150 ceiling.

The bundle's traffic advisory is absent, and I disclose that squarely: EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and can carry no fact. It costs the driver nothing here, because he asserts no external traffic cause at all, so POL-RD-13's testing regime is not engaged; and because no exculpatory clause is invoked against that identifier, its absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it and does not engage POL-RD-10(5).

The relief follows directly. The fare is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION leaves payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are — so on this rider-filed dispute the correct outcome is that the metered charge of 33.77 stands, and no money moves to the rider.

The rider's own arithmetic on the amount is unsupported: she asks $13.00 against a claim that the trip should have cost 'about $28', but she measures that $28 against a 21.0 km booking optimum that her own two amendments displaced. Measured against the route actually driven between the amended endpoints, the 33.77 charged is the metered charge on 26.17 km and 34.0 minutes, and the rider identifies no line of the fare breakdown that is overstated.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: the receipt distance you were worried about is not the distance the policy has to test. You moved the pickup pin to Punggol MRT yourself at 07:11:58 (recorded on the trip as a 07:12:30 amendment) and changed the destination from Terminal 1 to Terminal 3 at 07:41:40 (recorded as a 07:41:52 amendment). POL-RD-05 says that where an endpoint is amended after booking, the route-deviation test is re-run against the platform's re-quoted optimal for the amended endpoints, and that stored figure is 24.60 km / 31.0 minutes. Against that baseline, the trace distance of 26.17 km gives an excess of 1.57 km. POL-RD-01 needs BOTH limbs: more than 0.80 km (1.57 km passes) AND more than 20% of the optimal (1.57 / 24.60 = 6.4%, which fails). One limb passing is not enough, so no route deviation exists and, as POL-RD-05 states, the outcome is NO_ACTION. To the driver: the same re-basing disposes of the rider's $13.00 claim, and your own record supports it. The dropoff change to T3 was the rider's (chat MSG-00108-003), and your account of it matches the chat log and the trip record. The trace figure of 26.17 km, not the 26.2 km convenience copy on the receipt, is the governing measurement, and it is the trace that governs the threshold test. On the amount: the charge of SGD 33.77 is the metered charge on 26.17 km and 34.0 minutes; the rider's comparison to 'about $28' is measured against the 21.0 km booked optimum that her own two amendments displaced. On billing: the fare breakdown shows no ERP or toll lines and an airport surcharge of 0.00, which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, so there is nothing refundable under POL-RD-09. On the trace's own derived deviation block: it reports 'established' at 5.17 km / 24.6%, but it was computed against the booked optimum of 21.0 km, before either amendment; POL-RD-01 requires materiality to be assessed on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-05 adjustment, and after that adjustment no deviation survives. On the driver's traffic position: no external traffic cause was asserted, the bundle's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), and POL-RD-13 is not engaged; the driver invoked no exculpatory clause against a cited artifact, so no POL-RD-10(5) escalation arises. On POL-RD-04: every chat message carries waypoint_hint null and no road is named, so its 200 m corroboration test cannot be run; the clause is simply unavailable, and it is not needed, because POL-RD-05 already resolves the baseline. On the repeat-deviation check: with no deviation established and no material deviation on this trip, POL-RD-06 is not triggered; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 402, far below both the 3-flag and 5% tests. The driver's mention in passing of the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not a ground of decision — POL-GEN-01 makes that field context only, and POL-RD-06 asks for the trailing-90-day figure, which is what the claim actually used. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: all three artifacts carry TRP-00108, the trace is unimpaired (206 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), the POL-RD-05 re-quote is present and non-null, no fare line lacks a counterpart, and no refund amount is in issue. Confidence is capped at 1.0, the weight of the two artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-GPS-00108 trace and EV-TRIP-00108 amended re-quote, both at weight_multiplier 1.0), and I set it at 0.9. The metered charge of SGD 33.77 stands and no money moves.

To the rider and the driver: the metered charge of SGD 33.77 stands, and no money moves to either of you.

Why. The booking was Blk 118 Rivervale Drive to Changi Terminal 1, with a booked optimal of 21.0 km. The rider then moved the pickup pin to Punggol MRT (message 07:11:58, pin recorded amended at 07:12:30) and asked for Terminal 3 (message 07:41:40, dropoff recorded amended at 07:41:52). POL-RD-05 requires the deviation test to be re-run against the platform's re-quote between the AMENDED endpoints, which the trip record stores as amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km with amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0. That is a stored field; the tribunal does not re-derive it, and neither advocate disputed it.

The distance actually driven is the GPS trace length, 26.17 km. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, and the 26.2 km on the receipt and the trip record is a rounded convenience copy that may not be used for the threshold test. The trace is intact for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 206 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, at admissibility weight 1.0.

Against the amended 24.60 km, the excess is 26.17 - 24.60 = 1.57 km, which is 6.4% of the amended optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass: greater than 0.8 km absolute (cleared) AND greater than 20% of the optimal (failed). Because the percentage limb fails, no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's recomputation never runs, and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The driver advocate's position and the rider advocate's concession converge here, and I accept both: the derived deviation block on the GPS evidence reports status 'established' at 5.17 km and 24.6%, but that block was computed against the 21.0 km BOOKED optimum, before either amendment. It does not apply POL-RD-05 and does not govern. The residual 3.0 minutes of driving time (34.0 charged against 31.0 amended) is not an independent ground of refund; the policy's refund route (POL-RD-02) requires an established deviation, and there is none.

The 'five minutes driving around the airport' and the two loops of the T3 kerb sit inside the 1.57 km residual. Under POL-RD-05 that circling is excluded from excess where the rider was not at the amended point; whether it is excluded or counted, the residual remains under the 20% limb, so the point does not change the result. I record the rider advocate's disclosure that the derived arrival block is unavailable because pickup_zone_class is null, so the '>4 minutes' limb could not be computed; that does not affect the outcome.

The absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00108-01 (status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact, as both advocates disclosed. The driver asserts no external traffic cause, so POL-RD-13 is not engaged and no exculpatory clause is invoked against that identifier; its absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and POL-RD-10(5) does not fire.

No billing-integrity correction arises under POL-RD-09: the fare breakdown charges no ERP or toll lines, and the airport surcharge is 0.00, which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there.
